I haven't really used BitGo, but I'm kinda actively using Coinbase. However thanks to Choose your wallet at Bitcoin.org, I decided to keep most of my funds at GreenAddress. It's just that I don't like to trust big corps, moreover with my crypto funds. Oh yeah, and I've recently bought Ledger Wallet (HW wallet), which plays with GreenAddress nicely.

I'd suggest trying a few, maybe all of them (it's free after all) and decide what suits you best. That already mentioned "Choose your wallet" page is great for comparison and basic orientation in wallet differences.

Edit: I was looking for something multiplatform (Linux/Win at least + Android). Your requerements might be different..

Coinbase: you don't control your bitcoins, it's sort of a bank with a nice UI. If you create a Coinbase Vault, however, they control your bitcoins only partly (they hold one of the signatures required to send transactions). They also have AML/KYC procedures in place.

BitGo: you control your bitcoins partly as BitGo controls one of the signatures required to send funds.

Remember that if there is someone else in this world that has partial or full control of "your" bitcoins, those bitcoins are not yours. Alternatives, where you are in full control of your funds, include Electrum, Multibit, Armory, Mycelium, Bitcoin Wallet, Aitbitz and others.

For an everyday wallet, I'd say BitGo because you retain complete control of your funds while still getting the ease-of-use of a web-wallet (thanks to multisig). BitGo could disappear and you'd still have control of, and access-to, your funds.

Coinbase is good for buying bitcoin, but I hate storing much bitcoin with any service provider that could either freeze my account, or lose or steal my funds. All of those are a risk with Coinbase, but not with BitGo. The one exception is Coinbase's multisig vault product, which does give the user two of three keys (and thus ultimate control), but it's not designed to be an everyday wallet, whereas BitGo's default wallet is designed for normal use.
Why online wallets? There is little difference between them and the current banking system. Go with a lightweight local wallet.

Because It seriously messes you up if you don't. As a teenager I had some disorder for a while where I remembered most dreams. I couldn't tell which memories actually happened and which didn't. Drives you craze. Fortunately it stopped after a few weeks.
So why do some people train to lucid dreaming ? Wouldn't it have the same consequences ?
I'm not sure, but I think they still tend to forget their dreams, just not right away. They just remember them long enough to write them down.
I don't think so because when you're lucid dreaming you're aware that you're dreaming.

I've definitely woken up from a dream think "I've got to take care of this thing!", only to realize it was a dream... though a small part of me will still worry about it for a minute somewhere in the back of my head.

To go off of this. It's so that we're able to discern reality from non-reality. If we remembered our dreams just as strongly as we did our memories then what would stop people from believing their dreams actually happened. Most likely it's an evolutionary thing for self preservation.

That's a real deep question to be throwing down willy-nilly.
I think it's probably a few different things. For one, kids are expected to have some kind of dream when they're young, meant to be planning for the future when they barely have an understanding of what the world even is. You ask a kid "What do you want to be when you grow up?" and they try and guess what the right answer is because they don't know, but all the questions we ask them have a right answer, right? So there's gotta be something that they're meant to want to be, and they go "Oh I wanna be this thing that seems like something people like" or they list off the first thing that comes to their mind because they don't have a clue what the question even means. But then they've answered the question and people are unlikely to have told them "oh that's the wrong answer", so it must be the right one, right? And now all of a sudden you have an 8 year old kid who thinks they're meant to be a chef because they remember watching sesame street and thinking the hat looked funny, so they just said chef and everyone seemed to think that was the right answer, and adults are always right, man.
And then when you get older, you either pursue that dream you made up because you think that's right, forgetting what things actually make you happy in the process, or you get put into a 9-5 office job writing reports that you don't even think go anywhere and are too focussed on whether a winky face is appropriate for a business-casual inter-office email reminding people of the upcoming deadline to remember that at one point, you wanted to shoot off towards the stars.

But seriously, we forget our dreams because they're not important - they're just a little debugging tool the brain uses to check which bits are working and replace the faulty parts.
